We find that HII-CHI-Mistry returns systematically lower O/H and N/O values in shock-contaminated regions, especially for N/O, with typical offsets of ~0.1-0.15 dex relative to star-formation-dominated regions, together with a more homogeneous and lower ionisation state (log(U) ~ -3.1). In contrast, star-formation-dominated regions span a wider range of ionisation parameters (log(U) ~ -3.3 to -2.8) while maintaining approximately solar oxygen abundances. Despite these differences, the abundance offsets are comparable to the sampling step of the HII-CHI-Mistry model grid. The inferred oxygen abundance shows little variation between discs and halos. This is compatible with a scenario in which star formation feedback and galactic fountains efficiently recycle oxygen-rich gas between both components, in agreement with hydrodynamical simulations. In contrast, the N/O ratio shows significant radial and vertical variations, particularly in environments with weaker star formation feedback.

papers.title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
papers.abstract: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

papers.title: The ultraviolet continuum slopes of galaxies at $\mathbf{z \gtrsim 12}$ selected from ${\mathbf{0.6 \, deg}^2}$ of JWST imaging
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of the ultraviolet (UV) continuum slopes $(\beta)$ of $55$ galaxies at $z\gtrsim 12$, selected from a wide-area ($>0.6$ sq. deg) search across publicly available JWST/NIRCam imaging. Our sample spans the absolute UV magnitude ($M_{\mathrm{UV}}$) range $-21.6 \leq M_{\mathrm{UV}} \leq -17.3$ and we find an inverse variance-weighted mean $\langle\beta\rangle = -2.57\pm0.04$ indicating that, on average, the galaxy population is extremely blue at $z\gtrsim 12$. The average $\beta$ at these redshifts is consistent with the intrinsic stellar plus nebular continuum limit in the absence of UV dust-attenuation. Consistent with earlier JWST works, our analysis suggests that the moderately dust-attenuated galaxies at $z \lesssim 10$ become essentially attenuation-free by $z \simeq 11$. We find no evidence for a $\beta-M_{\mathrm{UV}}$ relation in our $z\gtrsim 12$ sample, indicating that the attenuation-free interpretation applies across all observed UV magnitudes. By augmenting our sample with previous JWST constraints down to $z=9$, and incorporating $M_{\mathrm{UV}}$-matched HST studies down to $z=4$, we find a smooth evolution in $\beta(z)$ over a wide range in redshift. The average value of $\beta$ becomes progressively bluer at $z>4$, with $\mathrm{d}\beta/\mathrm{d}z \simeq -0.1$. Finally, although we find that the typical galaxy at $z \gtrsim 12$ is consistent with the attenuation-free limit, the scatter in our individual $\beta$ measurements is consistent with the existence of a small population of dust-reddened galaxies with $\beta \gtrsim -2$.

papers.title: The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars
papers.abstract: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. Some GCE models with specific yield sets have been shown to reconcile predictions with observations. Here we re-analyse these yield sets to quantify the contribution of C-O shell mergers to K production and what the Galactic evolution of K implies about the occurrence of these events. We analyse 194 pre-supernova models from three independent yield sets, covering a wide range of initial masses, metallicities and rotational velocities, and including both single and binary-stripped stars. We identify the progenitors undergoing a C-O shell merger and compute GCE models with and without their contribution. In all three sets, the enhanced K production can be traced back to a small number of C-O merger progenitors, which eject up to ~10-50 times more K than non-merger progenitors of similar mass. Without them, no model reproduces the observations and [K/Fe] is sub-solar over most of the metallicity range. With them, [K/Fe] is enhanced only within the metallicity window where mergers occur in each grid. Binarity itself plays a minor role, as single stars alone produce similar amounts of K. Since the K synthesised in a C-O merger is essentially primary, the observed nearly linear increase of [K/H] with [Fe/H] can be reproduced only if C-O shell mergers occur with a similar frequency at all metallicities. K could therefore be used to infer the occurrence rate of C-O shell mergers in massive stars as a function of time.

papers.title: Radiation, Thermochemistry, and Stellar Feedback in DISPATCH
papers.abstract: The growth of massive stars depends on whether their accretion flows survive radiation and outflow feedback from the forming stellar population. We present an extension of DISPATCH that couples directional stellar radiation, diffuse infrared transport, and thermochemistry to self-gravitating magnetohydrodynamics, individual stellar accretion, and protostellar jets. This AMR-based method uses DISPATCH's local timestepping, allowing stellar environments and their larger scale cluster environments to step on separate timescales, and providing the framework needed to scale to long-duration simulations of GMCs. Direct radiation is transported in multiple bands, including both ionizing and nonionizing radiation, and uses short characteristics to maintain source directions and shadowing. Diffuse radiation is implemented for IR reprocessed light, with M1 and stationary ray options for transport. The thermochemical model includes atomic and molecular hydrogen and helium chemistry, and metal cooling and dust. It also includes a composition-dependent equation of state. Stellar masses grow through accretion of gas rather than a prescribed IMF, allowing stellar masses to respond to the evolving gas supply and feedback. In tests, multiple-source illumination retains geometric shadows while diffuse reprocessing heats shielded material, and tests of jets, ionization fronts, and radiation pressure demonstrate expected behavior and convergence. Ionization fronts also cross asynchronous refinement boundaries with late-time propagation speeds within a few percent of analytic predictions. Together, these developments provide a framework for determining how radiative and mechanical feedback modify the duration and efficiency of accretion from turbulent clouds, connecting the gas supply to individual stars with the high-mass stellar initial mass function.

papers.title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
papers.abstract: White dwarfs (WDs) provide a fossil record of the Milky Way star formation history (SFH) through the combined effects of stellar evolution and cooling. They have, however, generally been modelled in isolation from the non-degenerate population, so that no single self-consistent set of Galactic assumptions has been required to reproduce both. We present CALOMERA, a semi-analytic chemo-dynamical population synthesis framework in which the vertical density profiles of mono-age subpopulations are computed self-consistently with the Galactic potential and coupled to modern WD cooling sequences, metallicity-dependent progenitor lifetimes and synthetic photometry. We calibrate 18 parameters describing the initial mass function, SFH, initial-final mass relation and WD population against a Gaia DR3 sample of $7.98\times10^{6}$ stars within 1 kpc, including $1.1\times10^{5}$ WDs. The calibrated model reproduces the star counts in each colour-magnitude diagram region to within 3% and the total number count to within 0.5%, compared with the 81% excess in the predicted WD count obtained with the previous main-sequence-only calibration. The recovered SFH peaks early, declines exponentially thereafter, and includes two recent bursts, located at $\tau\approx2.4$ and $0.5$ Gyr. Three cooling libraries (Montr\'{e}al, BaSTI and LPCODE) yield comparably good fits, with differences confined to ${\rm M_G}\gtrsim15$ mag. The predicted luminosity function is in reasonable agreement with the 100 pc Gaia WD sample. We further predict the Galactic WD distribution and differential number counts for surveys of varying depth. Extending the framework to the substellar regime using ATMO models, we predict the Galactic L, T, and Y dwarf populations and their contribution to the deep JWST fields.

papers.title: MAHA-z: A Mahalanobis distance kNN estimator for photometric redshifts
papers.abstract: We present \texttt{MAHA-z}, a photometric-redshift (photo-$z$) estimator that combines $k$-nearest neighbour ($k$NN) regression with a Mahalanobis distance metric learned from the covariance of a spectroscopic reference sample. For each target galaxy, \texttt{MAHA-z} performs a neighbour search in a colour-magnitude feature space with optional morphological parameters, and returns both a point estimate and a redshift posterior $p(z\mid\mathbf{f})$ obtained by kernel density estimation over the neighbour redshifts. The Mahalanobis metric accounts for correlated features and heterogeneous units, eliminating ad hoc normalisation, and its subspace restriction allows \texttt{MAHA-z} to handle missing bands on a per-galaxy basis without imputation. We validate the method on four datasets spanning simulations and survey photometry: the Euclid Flagship~2 mock, the Legacy-KiDZ calibration sample, VIPERS, and the DES Year~3 BAO sample. On Euclid Flagship~2 (LSST+NISP) we achieve $\sigma_{\rm NMAD}=0.0148$ with a $0.27\%$ outlier fraction, and on DES Y3 we obtain $\sigma_{\rm NMAD}\approx0.023$ with $<1\%$ outliers and posterior calibration comparable to the \texttt{ANNz2} catalogue. \texttt{MAHA-z} processes millions of galaxies in minutes and provides competitive PDFs at substantially lower computational cost than trained machine-learning models, making it a practical option for iterative photo-$z$ production and validation in Stage-IV surveys.

papers.title: galpy with differentiable, accelerated backends: galactic dynamics in jax and PyTorch
papers.abstract: We describe an extension of galpy, the Python library for galactic dynamics, that adds jax and PyTorch as computational backends alongside its existing numpy and C implementation. With it, galpy's gravitational potentials, orbit integration, action-angle transformations and their inverses, and distribution functions, including those for tidal streams, run on GPUs, can be compiled as part of a user's program, and can be differentiated with respect to their inputs and parameters, from the force at a point to the samples drawn from a distribution function. The user-facing design is kept simple: the active backend follows from the type of the arrays that are passed in, the galpy interface is unchanged, and the numpy path gives the same results as before. We describe the design of the backend framework and its implementation in each of galpy's modules, with examples of use, and we discuss its limitations. On a GPU, batches of orbits, samples from distribution functions, and stream models run one to five orders of magnitude faster than on a single CPU core. To illustrate the new capabilities, we present simple examples of fitting the Galactic potential with a hypervelocity star and of learning the inverse action-angle transformation with a neural network trained through galpy. An AI coding agent wrote essentially all of the code under the detailed direction and review of the human author, and we describe how we organized this work and how we established the correctness of the result. This work is the start of galpy's version 2, which is available at https://github.com/jobovy/galpy and documented at https://docs.galpy.org/en/v2/ .

papers.title: Beyond classification: regressing physical merger properties using solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum
papers.abstract: Galaxy mergers play an important role in galaxy evolution; they enhance star formation, transform morphologies, and may drive accretion onto black holes. Due to their complex morphological features, identification of mergers poses a significant challenge. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been successful at identifying mergers with good accuracy. However, similar to other deep learning techniques such as Vision Transformers, they require large training samples. Current methods are also limited to classification, rather than regression. Here, we apply the solid harmonic wavelet scattering bispectrum, a method that encodes invariances and symmetries in the data which need to be learned by CNNs, as an alternative to CNNs. We apply our methodology to a simulated dataset of galaxies with a wide range of merger properties. We show that this method outperforms standard methodologies, while requiring fewer training samples and being robust to noise. Most importantly, we show that for the first time this method is able to regress on both merger mass ratio and time since merger simultaneously, with uncertainties ~ 0.33 dex uncertainty in merger mass ratio and ~ 0.66 Gyr uncertainty in time since merger. We have therefore shown that solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum presents an alternative to currently used machine learning techniques.

papers.title: Dark matter alters dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies
papers.abstract: Dwarf galaxies are the most dark-matter-dominated systems in the Universe, serving as unique laboratories for exploring the fundamental nature of the dark sector. Although the observed diversity in dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies suggests an interplay between dark matter and baryonic physics, this relationship has remained largely unquantified in existing models. Here, we utilize a set of novel cosmological simulations with baryons to demonstrate how dark matter physics directly drives the structural evolution of these galaxies. By comparing the same systems across cold dark matter and varied self-interacting dark matter models, we find that the evolution of the central density of dark matter significantly impacts a galaxy's half-light radius, but the signal is dependent on morphology. This causal link establishes galaxy size as a direct signature of the underlying dark matter microphysics. Our findings provide a predictive framework for decoding dark matter particle properties from galactic shapes, offering a roadmap for upcoming wide-field surveys, such as the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, to probe the dark sector through the statistical analysis of galaxy populations.

papers.title: Revisiting the distance to 4U 1543-475 through X-ray dust-scattering rings
papers.abstract: We derived a geometrical distance of the black-hole X-ray binary 4U 1543-475 based on X-ray dust-scattering rings associated with its 1992 and 2002 outbursts. We analyzed archival ROSAT and XMM-Newton observations and identified an X-ray dust-scattering ring in each observation, produced by two different dust layers along the line of sight. By combining the angular radii of the rings with the independently determined distances of the scattering dust layers and the epochs of the corresponding outbursts, we derive a best-constrained distance to 4U 1543-475 of 4.6 $\pm$ 0.2 kpc. This value is substantially smaller than the distance of 7.5 kpc commonly adopted in the literature and has important implications for the inferred physical properties of the system. In particular, the revised distance favors the presence of a low-mass extended-horizontal-branch donor star over a main-sequence star, calling for a reassessment of the dynamical parameters of the binary and, consequently, of the black-hole mass. The smaller distance also affects the inferred properties of the relativistic jet and the estimate of black-hole spin derived from the spectral continuum-fitting.

papers.title: Non-Gaussian matter fluctuations from primordial magnetic fields and galaxy luminosity function
papers.abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) represent a promising candidate for the origin of large-scale magnetic fields observed in astrophysical environments. Through the Lorentz force, PMFs generate matter density perturbations, leaving distinct imprints on the formation of cosmic structures. While previous studies have primarily characterized these imprints via the matter power spectrum --- a two-point statistic --- we demonstrate that the one-point statistics of PMF-induced density fluctuations reveal an intrinsically non-Gaussian probability distribution function (PDF), even when the PMFs themselves are statistically Gaussian. In particular, we find that the high-density tail of the PDF is enhanced by over two orders of magnitude relative to the Gaussian case. Adopting the Press-Schechter formalism, we show that this non-Gaussianity significantly boosts the abundance of rare objects, especially massive halos and those at high redshifts. We further compute the ultraviolet luminosity function of galaxies at $z=6$, $12$, and $16$, and compare our predictions with recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations that have reported an excess of high-redshift galaxies at $z\sim 12$ -- $16$ relative to standard $\Lambda$CDM expectations. Intriguingly, in the limiting case where the total density field inherits this PDF, our results suggest that the non-Gaussian density fluctuations sourced by PMFs can explain the bright-end ($M_\mathrm{UV}\lesssim -18$) excess at $z\gtrsim 12$, without requiring additional astrophysical enhancements to star-formation efficiency.

papers.title: LHAASO's Peanut source is a laboratory for studying magnetic fields in the Milky Way
papers.abstract: Recently, the LHAASO Collaboration reported gamma-ray emission from the Peanut-shaped source (Peanut), which extends over $4.5^\circ$ parallel to the Galactic plane at $b=-17.5^\circ$. The source is associated with the millisecond pulsar PSR J0218+4232, located at the eastern edge of the Peanut, at a distance of 3 kpc from the Earth and 0.9 kpc from the Galactic plane. Its location and bright gamma-ray emission above 25 TeV make it a natural laboratory for studying the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) in the transition region between the Galactic plane and halo. We interpret the observed emission as inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by electrons propagating along the large-scale GMF, accounting for turbulence through two models: Kolmogorov and Goldreich-Sridhar (GS). These models correspond to diffusive and ballistic particle propagation, respectively. While the GS case naturally provides conditions for one-sided gamma-ray emission, in the Kolmogorov case assumptions of one-sided particle injection and magnetic mirror at the source are necessary. We find that, in the Kolmogorov scenario, the Peanut's hotspots are likely associated with magnetic bottling, whereas in the GS scenario, they are related to magnetic field line geometry. Both models yield constraints on the GMF at the location of the Peanut.

papers.title: Euclid DR1 Legacy Science on Ultracool Dwarfs: Brown Dwarfs in the Blanco 1 Open Cluster
papers.abstract: A 35.6\,deg$^2$ field of Euclid Data Release~1 that covers part of the corona and tidal tails of the young (100--130\,Myr) nearby (234\,pc) open cluster Blanco~1 is presented. We select 22 ultracool dwarfs from Euclid photometry and slitless spectra, and measure proper motions over a median baseline of 13\,yr by combining Euclid astrometry with VIKING, KiDS and Rubin positions. Ten objects are comoving late-M and L dwarf candidates with membership probabilities of at least 0.5 under two field models. Nine of them are typed from their Euclid spectra, and the tenth is a candidate only if its colour-based type is adopted. Brown dwarf evolutionary models give masses of 0.03--0.06\,$M_\odot$ for the cluster age. The substellar population is about twice that predicted by a lognormal mass function scaled to the cluster's Gaia members. The remaining 12 objects are classified as late-M, L and T dwarfs with low probability of membership in the cluster. Using the Euclid sample to calibrate a search over 246\,deg$^2$ of VIKING and KiDS photometry and motions, we identify 60 ultracool candidates, with about seven expected by chance. In the core region of Blanco 1 archival Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam images and motions over 2011--2025 yield 35 candidates of types M7 or later, at least 20 of which are kinematic members at 95\% confidence. These results extend the spectroscopic sequence of Blanco 1 into the L-type brown dwarfs and the list of candidate members over the outskirts and tidal tails of the cluster.

papers.title: Dark Matter Velocimetry with Quantum Networks
papers.abstract: Quantum sensor networks can use the spatial phase coherence of wavelike dark matter to probe not only particle properties but also the motion and structure of the Galactic halo. We explore this idea for the minimal two-node network, in which a nonlocal exchange measurement samples the characteristic function of the velocity distribution. We compare the Standard Halo Model (SHM) with a Gaia-inspired radially anisotropic component and their mixture (SHM++), taking into account daily and annual modulation, postselection, depolarizing events, and a flat instrumental offset. We show that annual modulation at one fixed local sidereal time has the same phase waveform for the centered SHM and Gaia-inspired SHM++ models, leaving them degenerate when the overall signal amplitude is unknown. Earth's rotation breaks this degeneracy by scanning the baseline through Galactic directions and exposing the direction-dependent coherence of an anisotropic population. Distinguishing these velocity distributions would test whether the local halo is smooth and nearly isotropic or contains a radially biased accreted component, turning a quantum-network detection into a probe of Milky Way structure. Our likelihood analysis shows how modulation and signal-odd controls separate this information from flat backgrounds and provides a path from model discrimination toward measurement of the local velocity distribution.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NISP spectroscopy of gravitational arcs and multiple images
papers.abstract: Applications of strong gravitational lensing in astrophysics and cosmology critically depend on building reliable strong lensing models, which require accurate measurements of on-sky positions of multiple images and of the redshifts of the background sources from which they originate. In this context, Euclid is a unique facility, as it simultaneously provides high-resolution multi-band photometric imaging and slitless spectroscopy for an unprecedentedly large sample of gravitational lenses, most of which are newly discovered. In this work, we exploit Euclid slitless spectroscopic data to determine the redshifts of four spatially extended lensed sources, and to reconstruct emission-line images. Specifically, two of the target sources are lensed into giant arcs by the massive galaxy clusters SPT-CLJ0411$-$4819 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.424$, where "d" denotes the lensing deflector) and Abell 2280 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.326$). The third system is a quadruply imaged active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidate strongly lensed by a massive galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.68$, while the fourth is a galaxy-scale Einstein ring produced by a lens galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.235$. This work represents a proof of concept for the exploitation of Euclid slitless spectroscopic data in the study of strong gravitational lensing, providing one of the first determinations of spectroscopic redshifts for strongly lensed features from NISP spectra. These results demonstrate the feasibility of applying the same methodology to the very large sample of gravitational lenses that Euclid has started to discover and is expected to identify over the course of the mission.

papers.title: A Multi-Cycle Treasury Survey of Andromeda: Comprehensive, All-Encompassing Spectroscopy, Imaging, and Mid-Infrared Mapping of the Nearest Giant Spiral
papers.abstract: We propose a Multi-Cycle Treasury program of $\sim$800 hours that would survey Andromeda the way the Milky Way has been surveyed by APOGEE, Gaia, and WISE. - NIRSpec: spectra of $\sim$4,500 red giants and supergiants at S/N~80, sufficient for 16 elements at $\lesssim$0.05 dex precision and radial velocities to a few km s$^{-1}$. - NIRCam: $\sim$1,600 arcmin$^{2}$ in up to ten filters, reaching $\sim$20 million stars, every field imaged twice a year apart: two-epoch infrared photometry of the $\sim$500 Cepheids and $\sim$10$^{4}$ Miras in the footprint. - MIRI: $\sim$450 arcmin$^{2}$ in five filters at the depth of PHANGS. The observations are predominantly organized as twelve "bricks", each of three adjacent fields including two NIRSpec/MOS pointings, in which one instrument is prime and a second observes in parallel, so that roughly 40% of the exposure time comes at no charge. The bricks sample the nucleus, bulge, major axis to 29 kpc, minor axis, and inter-arm disk. In addition, a 100-hour grid of short NIRCam pointings with MIRI in parallel covers the HST-PHAT footprint. The result would be the first chemodynamical, star-formation, and dust map of an $L^{\star}$ galaxy other than our own built from individual stars, at a scale no single-cycle program can reach.

papers.title: Sailing with the winds of HL Tau: the JWST view
papers.abstract: Studying protostellar ejections is crucial to understanding the formation of young stars and planetary systems. The Class I/II star HL Tau, with its ringed disk and prominent bipolar outflows, is a benchmark system for these studies. We provide a first overview of our Cycle 3 JWST program targeting HL Tau, focusing on the morphology and kinematics of the various wind components as well as on the water emission lines excited in the inner disk. Our observations cover the 1.66-28 $\mu$m spectral range, combining NIRSpec and MIRI MRS mosaics to map the inner 10" of the red-shifted lobe of the outflow and the base of the blue-shifted lobe. In the red-shifted lobe we observe a stratified wind of three nested layers: a fast, highly collimated atomic jet structured in a chain of eight knots and with radial velocities of 160 km/s; a wide-angle H$_2$ wind with velocities of 45 km/s exhibiting complex arc-like substructures; and a warm gas shell, of radial velocity of 35 km/s, visible in low-excitation transitions of CO ($\nu$=1-0). This CO shell appears co-spatial with the CO (J=2-1) emission detected by ALMA with velocities from 3 to 25 km/s. In the first 1" of the blue-shifted lobe we detect a similar stratification, but the jet is faster and less collimated. The observed stratification and kinematics of the flow may support a magnetically driven disk-wind scenario in which the distinct components originate in the disk at progressively larger distances from the star. However, while the external components observed in CO have the laminar and regular appearance predicted for such winds, the knots in the inner jet and the arcs in the wind could be the manifestation of a pulsed ejection mechanism. Additionally, in MIRI spectra taken at the star position we detect a forest of water lines dominated by cold-to-warm (< 500 K) gas. Their distribution suggests an extended reservoir of sublimated ices.

papers.title: A flash before dawn: 21 cm signatures of transient reionization from supermassive Pop III stars
papers.abstract: Recent data from cosmological galaxy surveys combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data give a preference for a departure from $\Lambda$CDM, favoring a model with an evolving dark energy equation of state or a small neutrino mass. However, recent works have shown that the electron scattering optical depth to the CMB ($\tau$) can reduce this preference if $\tau\sim0.09$, larger than that preferred by CMB low-$\ell$ E-mode polarization data. With standard monotonic hydrogen reionization histories, such a high value of $\tau$ is in strong tension with spectroscopic galaxy data constraining the end of reionization. Thus, high-$\tau$ models are restricted to non-standard reionization scenarios, where astrophysical sources inject an appreciable amount of ionizing photons at early times. One recently studied model for this is a supermassive population III star scenario, where radiative feedback from a self-annihilating dark matter particle enables a pathway to form $M\sim10^5 M_\odot$ stars that, upon collapse, photoionize a surrounding volume large enough to source appreciable contributions to $\tau$ as a population. Here we present the first self-consistent treatment of the feedback from these supermassive population III stars within a large semi-numerical cosmological simulation, accounting for their ionizing, Lyman-Werner, and X-ray feedback on the intergalactic medium. We use it to predict the distinct signatures on the large-scale 21 cm signal at Cosmic Dawn, and forecast its detectability. We find that the 21 cm power spectrum probed by future radio survey arrays like the Square Kilometre Array could detect signatures of these supermassive population III at high significance and set model-dependent constraints on $\tau$ that approach $\sigma_\tau\sim0.012$, enough to distinguish our fiducial $\tau\sim0.097$ scenario from current Planck values at $>3\sigma$.

papers.title: The ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR): Initial Data Release (DR1)
papers.abstract: The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) has observed the northern sky observable from Palomar Observatory since March 2018, accumulating a median of a thousand photometric measurements across $gri$ for each of more than a billion sources. Among these billions of objects are millions of periodically variable stars, active galactic nuclei, stellar remnants, and substellar objects. We describe the initial data release (DR1) of the ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR) which provides image difference forced photometry, candidate periods, and variability metrics for approximately 1.3 billion sources in ZTF having an identification in Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (PS1). The data cover the 5.37 year interval between March 2018 and July 2023. ZVAR is sensitive to periods between 5 minutes and 2.7 years. We also describe tools for accessing the ZVAR data.

papers.title: 3D radiative transfer of K-series lines of He-like ions with SKIRT
papers.abstract: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy with XRISM has resolved line profiles of highly ionised ions, including P Cygni profiles, in many systems containing compact objects. To interpret these line profiles, forward modelling with three-dimensional radiative transfer (3D RT) calculations including the relevant ionic processes is required. Following our previous work on the Lyman-series lines of H-like ions, we present the implementation of the K-series lines of He-like ions with Z = 2-30 in the open-source Monte Carlo RT code SKIRT, providing a numerical tool for interpreting highresolution X-ray spectra of photoionised plasmas. Building upon the framework developed for H-like ions, we incorporate the resonance scattering (RS) and radiative recombination (RR) channels. We also implement the inner-shell ionisation (II) channel of Li-like ions for the production of He-like lines. We resolve fine-structure levels and account for level populations, frequency redistribution, phase function, and linear polarisation through transition-specific Mueller matrices. The implementation reproduces the expected RT effects in He-like lines. The Fe xxv w and y lines, dominated by the RS channel, develop optically thick line-profile distortions and P Cygni profiles in an outflowing plasma, whereas the x and z lines, dominated by the RR and II channels, do not exhibit such behaviour. The line intensities from the RS and RR channels agree well with Cloudy. The II channel further enhances the z line, which is not yet included in Cloudy. The linear polarisation calculations reproduce the analytical and experimental angular dependence of resonance scattering on a line-by-line basis. This extension to He-like lines, together with our previous implementation of H-like lines, enables 3D RT modelling of the major X-ray lines, providing a tool for constraining gas kinematics around compact objects observed with XRISM.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Colouring Euclid with external ground-based imaging data
papers.abstract: Accurate photometric-redshift estimation and calibration of the weak-lensing point-spread function (PSF) for Euclid require complementary ground-based optical imaging with high photometric precision and spatial homogeneity. The Organisation Unit for External Data (OU-EXT) integrates heterogeneous ground-based surveys into the Euclid Science Ground Segment (SGS), delivering uniformly calibrated, co-added images, and associated PSF models. To minimise systematics in spectral energy distribution (SED) reconstruction and photometric-redshift estimation, these data must achieve relative photometric stability at the $\sim$10 mmag level on Euclid-tile scales. We present the ground-based imaging component of Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), comprising $\sim2500$ deg$^2$ across the wide, deep, and auxiliary fields. We summarise the OU-EXT production workflow and validation framework, and quantify the achieved data quality of the co-added products in terms of depth, photometric zero-point stability, and spatial colour homogeneity. In the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS), the point-source $10\sigma$ depths in the $griz$ bands reach 24.8/24.3/24.0/23.0 AB mag, with the deep fields extending 1--2 magnitudes deeper. Most EWS DR1 tiles meet the 10 mmag relative photometric requirement, with 1.1% and 1.5% showing offsets exceeding 50 mmag in the northern and southern hemispheres, respectively. Spatial colour variations remain typically below 5--10 mmag across the southern EWS footprint, while larger residual structures of 10--25 mmag appear in some northern regions. These results demonstrate that the EXT production chain provides a largely homogeneous framework for integrating ground-based datasets into Euclid, while identifying calibration and co-addition limitations that have to be addressed in DR2 to meet the mission's most stringent cosmological requirements. (Abridged)

papers.title: Radiative Transfer Modeling of Multi-Shell Molecular Outflows in the Class 0 Protostar IRAS 15398-3359
papers.abstract: Recent high-angular-resolution observations of protostellar outflows have revealed complex spatial and velocity structures that are difficult to describe with a single shell. We have investigated the primary outflow of the Class 0 protostar IRAS 15398$-$3359 in the H$_2$CO and CS emission observed with ALMA and identified four shell-like components, which trace the cavity walls of the more extended CO outflows. Non-LTE radiative-transfer calculations of H$_2$CO and synthetic ALMA observations of the three-dimensional model show that a common ellipsoidal geometrical form and Hubble-law-like velocity field can broadly reproduce the channel-map and position--velocity structures of the identified shells when the geometry, spatial configuration, and kinematics of each shell are allowed to vary independently. The kinematic timescales and inclination angles of the inner and outer shells are $\sim$1000 yr ($19^\circ$ and $15^\circ$) and $\sim$750 yr ($5^\circ$ and $8^\circ$), respectively. The momentum injection rate of the outer bipolar pair is approximately 2.2 times that of the inner pair. The inferred $\dot{M}_{\rm wind}/\dot{M}_{\rm acc}$ ratios are $0.7$--$3\%$ and $2$--$7\%$ for the inner and outer shells. The observed shell-to-shell differences suggest episodicity of the mass ejection events, where the strength and direction of the outflow activity may vary over short timescales of order $10^2$--$10^3$ yr.

papers.title: A deterministic theory of kinetic fluctuations in long-range interacting homogeneous systems without collective effects
papers.abstract: Finite-$N$ fluctuations govern the slow relaxation of long-range interacting systems, yet accessing their full statistics demands huge ensembles of costly simulations. We show that, in homogeneous systems without collective effects, this statistical problem collapses onto just three deterministic kinetic equations. Starting from the Landau-Dean-Kawasaki equation, i.e. the stochastic counterpart of the large deviation principle for the Landau equation, we derive the infinite hierarchy of $n$-point moments of the empirical distribution function at leading order in $1/N$. We prove that it is solved exactly by a quasi-Gaussian closure. The resulting minimal Landau fluctuation hierarchy is formed by the Landau equation, a Lyapunov equation for the two-point moment, and a kinetic equation for the three-point moment. From these three equations, all higher-order moments follow algebraically. The hierarchy exactly preserves the collisional invariants and their fluctuations, and predicts the full probability distribution of observables in the central fluctuation regime. Benchmarked against $N$-body realizations, it reproduces the mean, variance and higher-order moments with an accuracy that improves systematically with $N$. A single deterministic time-integration of three coupled partial differential equations thus replaces large ensembles of simulations, for any large $N$.

papers.title: A Variable Compact Millimeter Excess in the Type-1 Seyfert Galaxy NGC 985: Implications for a Black-Hole Corona
papers.abstract: Compact millimeter emission from radio-quiet active galactic nuclei has been proposed as a probe of magnetized accretion-disk coronae. We present three epochs of ALMA observations of the type-1 Seyfert galaxy NGC 985, together with archival post-upgrade VLA data presented here for the first time, to investigate its compact millimeter excess. The millimeter flux density decreased strongly between the first two ALMA epochs separated by approximately one month, while the component was detected again at an intermediate level in the third epoch. This variability demonstrates an intrinsically variable compact component and implies a model-independent size limit of $\lesssim 0.024$ pc ($\simeq 1.1\times10^3 R_{\rm S}$). Spectral decomposition requires a compact, self-absorbed synchrotron component to reproduce the millimeter-wave data. A hybrid thermal/nonthermal coronal model reproduces the radio-millimeter spectra, with the two broadly sampled ALMA epochs favoring different nonthermal electron distributions. The estimated radiative cooling times are comparable to or shorter than the light-crossing time, implying continuous injection or reacceleration of nonthermal electrons; a change in particle injection is the most natural driver of the observed spectral changes. We conclude that NGC 985 hosts a recurrent and variable compact millimeter synchrotron component. A magnetized corona provides a plausible origin, although the present data do not uniquely distinguish a coronal origin from alternatives such as a jet base.
